findings.title: Admin embeddable hosts controller has no authorization on destroy/update lookup and uses unchecked nil
findings.body: The update and destroy actions look up the host with EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first and never check for nil. A request for a non-existent id causes a NoMethodError (500) on host.destroy or save_host. Also the ensure_staff filter is inherited but the create/update path assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] without a nil check, so a request missing the embeddable_host key raises a 500 instead of a 400/404.

findings.title: Embedding update action does not persist anything
findings.body: The update action just re-renders the serialized embedding and never saves changes. The admin UI calls embedding.update({}) expecting changes to be saved, but nothing is persisted, so the 'Save' path silently discards data. Host edits go through the separate embeddable_hosts resource, so this endpoint is effectively a no-op.

findings.title: before_validation mutates host with sub! which fails on nil
findings.body: self.host.sub! is called on the host attribute without a nil check. If host is nil (e.g. a POST without a host param, since save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] directly), this raises NoMethodError instead of producing a validation error. The sub! also mutates the string in place, which can alter frozen or shared strings.

findings.title: Host lookup lowercases only the stored column comparison, not the input host
findings.body: record_for_host compares lower(host) to the raw uri.host without downcasing it. A referer or embed URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com/page) will not match a stored host, so it is rejected, while the stored value is normalized to lowercase only in the query. Downcase the input host before querying.

findings.title: Category falls back to nil silently when no embeddable host matches
findings.body: category: eh.try(:category_id) passes nil when the URL host has no EmbeddableHost record, and the migration/allow-list logic no longer uses a configured default category. PostCreator then places the topic in the default category handling rather than failing, and the record_for_host lookup for a URL with a path or port may differ from the host check in EmbedController, so imports can land in unexpected categories.

findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent
findings.body: The query selecting category id from embed_category uses [0]['id'] on the result. If no matching row exists, [0] is nil and ['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration on installs that never set embed_category. Also the host values are interpolated directly into SQL without escaping, so a host containing a quote breaks the migration or allows SQL injection from existing setting data.

findings.title: Saved category is set from a possibly stale id and the new-host flow is broken
findings.body: After save, host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(...)) runs, but for a newly created host, the buffered host value is not reflected in the record, and cancel() on a new record calls deleteHost without removing server state. Also save() passes props including only 'host' via getProperties, so category_id from categoryId is merged but the rollback on error is never performed.

findings.title: Type normalization replaces only the first underscore
findings.body: type.replace('_', '-') only replaces the first underscore, so a type with multiple underscores will not match ADMIN_MODELS. Use a global replace or normalize consistently.

findings.title: Test asserts expandable behavior that was changed without covering the new contract
findings.body: The expandable_first_post? tests were restructured, but the removed case that checks behaviour when embeddable hosts are absent is now only covered by a test that creates no host with a misnamed describe ('emeddable'). The embed_truncate-only path (no host) is not clearly asserted after the SiteSetting change, leaving the new contract untested.

findings.title: Embedding host label reads incorrectly
findings.body: The 'host' label 'Allowed Hosts' and the 'edit' string are lowercase while sibling keys are capitalized; the confirm_delete text says 'that host' without naming it. Minor, but the strings are user-facing in the admin UI.
